_doc: High crowns (systems/highCrowns.js): holding more than one crown in personal union, the viceroys who rule the far crowns, the lords who want a king of their own, proclaiming an Empire or High Kingship, and the choice at succession to keep the crowns whole or partition them among the younger children. Days: 120 to the year.

levy._doc: A far crown's levy to your purse: its tax policy's share of the crown's daily dues (as the home crown's), times share, scaled by the realm's stability and lowered by separatism; never below the treasury's reserve; at most cap a day. A disloyal viceroy keeps part of it.

viceroy._doc: Kinds: spouse, kin (a grown child or sibling of the House), courtier (of systems/court.js), native (a great lord of that realm's own council). Loyalty settles toward a target from the House's Prestige, your favours and your visits, and sinks with neglect; competence moves the realm's stability and taxes; a disloyal viceroy skims the levy into his own purse; a disloyal, ambitious one plots and at last crowns himself.

separatism._doc: 0-100: how much a far crown's lords want a king of their own. Weekly change in points. Read by the realm's stability (crown.mods), the levy, the viceroy's loyalty and the breakaway.

presence._doc: Standing anywhere in a far crown's realm counts as a royal progress.

inherit._doc: A realm's royal line fails or wavers (an AI succession) while you hold a claim of blood or marriage on it: its council may offer you the crown in personal union. chance = clamp((claim - minClaim) / span) x the cause's factor x maxChance.

dictate._doc: Your crown at war with a realm whose capital you once stormed (a conquest claim), its host broken: dictate the crown to its court.

proclaim._doc: Proclaiming an Empire or High Kingship: needs minCrowns crowns, minPrestige, minSettlements across them; costs prestigeCost and the coronation feast (gold, into the capital's town, half from the purse and half from the home crown's chests at most). Lasting: yearlyPrestige, stability to every crown, envoys' regard; new problems: separatism x separatism.empireMult, the leagues' fear and resolve.

succession._doc: At a succession with far crowns: 'whole' keeps every crown for the heir (each far crown's separatism +wholeSpike; the younger children grow aggrieved); 'partition' gives each far crown, in order, to a grown younger child of the House (they rule it as kin: allied, warm, a cadet crown). A child heir: +minorSpike.

power._doc: Coalitions.power: each far crown counts as crownShare of a crown and its towns; an Empire adds empire.

court._doc: Each far crown's own royal court (systems/kingship.js run through Kingship.withCourt): vassals, a council headed by the viceroy, edicts sharing the law slots with the decrees, factions and revolts. opinion: what its lords add to their opinion of the crown (absence per year past absentAfterDays, capped; present; a foreign king; the viceroy by kind plus (competence - 50) x viceroyCompetence; separatism past separatismPivot x separatism). demands: at nativeKingAt separatism a lord of opinion <= nativeKingOpinion bands for a king of their own; at nativeViceroyAt for a native viceroy. separatism (points a week): -mean opinion x opinion, + each native-king faction's threat x faction, + revolt (x1.5 for a native king); league wars: townLost per town taken, warLost / warWon per war ended; a revolt crushed: crushed (native king) or quelled. conceded: granting a king of their own ends the union in peace (relations, Prestige lost).

titles._doc: The high title by the home crown's culture: male, female, the realm word ("Empire of Valdoria").

decrees._doc: Each far crown may keep up to slots decrees, proclaimed for Prestige. mods go to the realm (KingdomBonuses via kingdom.crown.mods); separatism is points a week; levy multiplies the far crown's levy.

charter.label: Confirm the ancient charter
charter.blurb: Swear to keep the realm's old laws and liberties. Its lords are soothed; your levy from it is smaller.

garrisons.label: Royal garrisons
garrisons.blurb: Your soldiers in its castles. Order and fewer plots; its treasury pays the soldiers 4 gold a day.

tribute.label: Tribute to the high crown
tribute.blurb: The realm sends more of its dues to you. Your purse fills; its lords grumble that they serve a foreign king.

native_court.label: Native lords at court
native_court.blurb: Offices of the realm only for its own born. Its lords are content; your viceroy's hand is tied.

text.offer: The royal line of {realm} has faltered. Its council remembers your claim of {claim} and offers you its crown, to wear beside your own.
text.coronation: In the great hall of {seat}, before the lords of {crowns}, {name} is crowned {title} of the {realmWord} of {proper}. {crownCount} crowns are one name now.
text.breakaway: The lords of {realm} will serve a foreign king no longer. They crown {ruler} at {seat}; the union is broken.
text.usurp: {viceroy}, your viceroy in {realm}, has crowned himself at {seat}. The union is broken.
text.partition: As the old {title} wished, the crowns are parted: {list}.
